- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model tends to overshoot — reduce forecast by 5–15% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7) and forecast is trending upward, check for mean reversion — if price has been rising for 5+ days, cap forecast at 1–2 std dev above recent mean.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast (especially after 10–15 days), apply downward bias correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day of lag.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., +1.0 → -0.5 → +0.5), model overfits momentum — dampen forecast by 10–20% for next 3 days.
